evidence: Automated dependency-update tooling (Dependabot or Renovate) is configured, so vulnerable dependencies surface as pull requests instead of waiting for a human to notice
expected_output: One observation row with dependabot, renovate, automated, config

assertions.description: A dependency-update automation config exists (.github/dependabot.yml or a Renovate config).

notes: Empty-set discipline — Witness: repo-facts always emits exactly one row carrying the `automated` boolean, so a repo with no update automation violates honestly rather than passing over zero rows; an empty observation set here could only mean the collector never ran.

plain.checks: Looks for a Dependabot or Renovate configuration — a robot whose job is to open a pull request when a dependency you use publishes a new version.
plain.violation: Nothing brings fixes to you. Vulnerable dependencies stay exactly where they are until a person happens to look, which in practice means until a scan like this one finds them.
plain.fix: Add .github/dependabot.yml or a Renovate config covering each package ecosystem in the repository, and decide who reviews what it opens — automation whose pull requests nobody merges is not automation.
